title: Choose Panel’s new visual world
question: Each direction preserves the full product while changing how the team reads and operates it.

options.label: Topology Atlas
options.lineage: network topology atlases and infrastructure maps
options.thesis: Panel becomes a calm operational atlas where servers, customers, and subscription paths read as one connected system.
options.viewport: A narrow command rail frames a live operational field, with health summaries above a precise queue of users and servers.
options.risk: The map logic can become ornamental unless every connector carries real meaning.

raised.raise: Critical quantities receive unmistakable fixed-position emphasis.
Every divider, bracket, and alignment follows one rigorous ruling system.
The construction grid remains visibly structural instead of becoming generic cards.

options.label: NOC Shift Board
options.lineage: network operations centers and shift handover boards
options.thesis: The dashboard behaves like a beautifully disciplined shift board: current state, exceptions, and next actions always visible.
options.viewport: A high-signal overview pairs large system health with a compact exception queue and direct operational shortcuts.
options.risk: It is the most familiar operational direction and needs exceptional typography to avoid standard dark-dashboard territory.

options.label: Ruling Engine Ledger
options.thesis: Panel becomes a precise operational ledger with a fixed action rail and annotation margins for exceptions.
options.viewport: Dense customer and server records sit in measured columns around a fixed rail of actions and states.
options.case: Wins on product clarity and density discipline; audience identification is less immediate than a network-native atlas.
options.risk: Long Persian labels may strain the strict column measure if the responsive rules are not exact.

options.label: Visible Systems Grid
options.thesis: A visible modular grid makes the system’s structure and hierarchy impossible to miss.
options.viewport: A monumental health statement anchors an openly gridded field of task modules and live records.
options.case: Matches product clarity through rigorous hierarchy; identification is more design-cultural than reseller-native.
options.risk: Oversized constructed type could consume space needed by operational data.

options.label: Nixie Instrument Bank
options.thesis: Every operational quantity becomes a glowing physical counter in a blackened instrument rack.
options.viewport: Fixed banks of glowing counts dominate above compact server and customer controls.
options.case: Memorable for monitoring, but weak for frequent forms, tables, and long Persian content.
options.kept: Quantities deserve fixed positions and unmistakable emphasis.
options.risk: The physical metaphor overwhelms routine administration.

options.label: Phosphor Operations Grid
options.thesis: The control panel becomes a strict luminous tile system with sprite-like state changes.
options.viewport: A tile-perfect status field presents metrics, alerts, and routes as one luminous operating screen.
options.case: Strong state language, but the game association undermines trust for customer operations.
options.kept: State colors operate as strict laws rather than decoration.
options.risk: It can feel playful when the team needs authority and calm.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished modern SaaS admin dashboard with familiar cards, sidebar navigation, and blue status accents.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional sidebar surrounds summary cards, charts, and recent activity.
canonCard.risk: Easy to learn, but intentionally resembles many existing admin products.
